title: Dressing the table before a game
target: How the play table in TCG Card Shop Simulator is put together: the table keeps a set of items, the playmat and the deck box are meshes of their own, and the build ships several sleeve and dice pictures to dress them with.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A play table in the shop

steps.do: Treat the table as a set of parts rather than one object, because the table keeps a set of items with its own data.
steps.because: the table keeps a set of items with data of its own (TableGameItemSet, TableGameItemSetData, m_TableGameItemSetData)

steps.do: Lay the playmat as its own piece, because it has a mesh of its own rather than being painted on the table.
steps.because: a playmat has a mesh of its own (m_PlayMatMesh, m_Mesh_Playmat)

steps.do: Watch the mat darken when the game needs the screen calm, because the background darkens behind it.
steps.because: the playmat background can be darkened (m_DarkenPlaymatBG)

steps.do: Put the deck in a box rather than loose, because the deck box is a mesh with a filter of its own.
steps.because: a deck box has a mesh and a filter of its own (m_DeckBoxMesh, m_DeckBoxMeshFilter)

steps.do: Choose the box that fits the deck, because the build ships several box designs including a nine-up tower and a six-up penny-sleeve box.
steps.because: the game ships more than one deck box design (T_DeckBox, T_DeckBox4, T_9_UP_TowerDeckbox, T_6_UP_PennySleeves)

steps.do: Sleeve the deck in the design you want, because there are sleeves for wind, fire and earth, for the game's own set, and a plain second design.
steps.because: sleeve artwork exists for several designs (T_CardSleeveWind, T_CardSleeveFire, T_CardSleeveEarth, T_CardSleeveTetramon, CardSleeve_second)

steps.do: Keep the dice with the table, because the game ships dice artwork and a dice box for it.
steps.because: the game ships dice artwork and a dice box (T_D20Dice, Icon_Dice_Yellow, DiceBox_second)

steps.do: Leave an empty slot visible rather than filling every place, because an empty playmat slot has a picture of its own.
steps.because: there is a picture for an empty playmat slot (Icon_EmptyPlaymat)

commonMistakes: Treating the playmat as part of the table and never changing it.
Putting a deck in a box that does not fit how it is sleeved.
Forgetting that the mat can darken while a game is on.
Leaving no empty slot for a card that is on its way.
Mixing sleeves between decks that are meant to stay apart.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Identifiers are listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
